title: Historical V54 - Maintenance Guide
summary: How to keep authored docs, legacy docs, generated references, tests, and launch scripts healthy.
html:
Historical reference. See the current V55 architecture guide before using this material.

Maintenance Guide

Keep the manual useful by preserving three layers: readable authored docs, historical legacy source material, and generated references that make drift visible. The served manual is canonical for current behavior.

Updating Authored Pages

Add Markdown files under src/manual/content. Include frontmatter with id, title, kind, tags, summary, and order.

Use slug-only document IDs:

lowercase-letters-numbers-and-dashes

Updating Legacy Docs

Legacy docs are copied from root docs/ into src/manual/content/legacy. The loader infers metadata when no frontmatter exists. Treat these pages as historical context, not the product source of truth. When behavior changes, update authored manual pages first and leave legacy copies only when older architecture notes are intentionally preserved.

Checking Generated Pages

Generated references inspect source files under:

  • src/agent_runtime
  • src/audio_runtime
  • src/gateway_agent
  • src/gateway_core
  • src/llm

Caches, artifacts, virtual environments, vendored files, and binaries are skipped.

Curated references such as System Surfaces And API Reference are authored manually and should be updated whenever routes, standalone pages, settings preferences, or UI drawer behavior changes. Generated references make source drift visible, but they do not replace the curated reader-facing API map. For Gmail changes, update the Gmail Integration manual page, Gmail Integration Architecture, System Surfaces And API Reference, Configuration And Storage, and any website cards that link to data-manual-doc="gmail-integration".

Test Commands

python -m pytest tests/test_manual_service.py
bash -n setup-manual.sh startmanual.sh

Release Checklist

  • Manual opens at /manual.
  • Health returns mode: manual.
  • Search works with and without FTS5.
  • Legacy docs appear in the catalog.
  • Legacy docs are labeled historical in the catalog and maintenance guidance.
  • The current browser surfaces and API groups are represented in System Surfaces And API Reference.
  • Gmail routes, account scoping, cache storage, OAuth configuration, and confirmation-gated mutations are represented when Gmail code changes.
  • Root docs and served manual pages agree on settings persistence, standalone pages, drawers, and immersive-mode behavior.
  • Generated route and environment pages reflect source changes.
  • Mermaid diagrams render locally.
